newsitem.title: DUBAI: Welcome Break puts Investcorp in limelight.
newsitem.headline: Welcome Break puts Investcorp in limelight.

text.p: The announcement on Tuesday by British hotels and leisure group Granada Group Plc that it had agreed to sell Welcome Break Ltd to Bahrain's Investcorp has pushed the Gulf company back into the limelight.

Fifteen years after Investcorp Bank EC was founded on the small Gulf island, its reputation has spread across the globe as a first rate investment bank with a taste for luxury and the skill to turn crumbling companies into cash cows.
The firm, with offices in Manama, London and New York, was formed in 1982 to service the needs of cash-rich investors in oil-rich Gulf.

But high-profile acquisitions and sales of prestigious companies such as jeweller Tiffany & Co and Italian luxury goods maker Gucci helped make Investcorp known far beyond the Gulf. Welcome Break motorway service stations, bought for 476 million stg, was the most recent purchase on a long list.

"Since inception, Investcorp has established a very strong track record in originating, structuring, placing and exiting profitably from complex and sophisticated direct investment transactions," said Martin Gallagher, banking analyst at specialist bank rating agency Capital Intelligence (CI).
Analysts say success lies in the firm's skill at buying struggling companies at a bargain price, injecting capital and restructuring their debt before reselling them at a profit.

"Most of Investcorp's companies come in quite sick," an analyst said. "Investcorp applies management expertise, gets in the experienced personnel from the industry and becomes very supportive, providing finance to these companies."
Investcorp management committee member Salman Abbasi said the key to success was different.

"We are not specialised in sick companies," he said. "We look for investments which have good management, track record and cashflow. We acquire them and then work with management to add value and then we sell them with reasonable returns."
He said Welcome Break had good assets, management and was well-established. "We think that we can add value," he said.
Abbasi said success also stemmed from a high degree of specialisation, adding that the company's emphasis on acquisitions in North America and Europe would continue.
"The market has great depth and we are still working on establishing ourselves very well in Europe," he said.

The company said net profit rose by a hefty 28.6 percent to $90.4 million thanks to the full realisation of three corporate investments and the partial realisation of two others. The firm also made three new corporate and two real estate investments during the year.

The company and its clients currently own 13 corporate investments in North America and Europe, including upmarket retailer Saks Fifth Avenue, Swiss watchmaker Ebel and U.S. bedding manufacturer Simmons Company.
Investcorp SA, the group's primary global asset holding company, is located in Luxembourg. The bank has an authorised capital of $500 million of which $100 million has been issued and fully paid.

But analysts say the picture is not all rosy. CI said in a recent report that the company lacked specific disclosure regarding provisions for the permanent diminution in value of investments, and non-performing assets in general.
